subChunks.title: Colour and Typography
subChunks.hookHtml: A developer who can reach for the right shade of gray instantly, set a typographic hierarchy in under a minute, and understand why text-blue-600/75 means 75% opacity — that developer ships UI significantly faster than one who guesses hex codes.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
The colour palette

Tailwind ships 22 colour families. Each family has 11 shades: 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900, 950.

  • 50 — near white. Good for page backgrounds.
  • 100–200 — light tints. Good for subtle card backgrounds, chips.
  • 400–600 — vivid mid-range. Good for buttons, links, icons.
  • 700–800 — dark shades. Good for text on light backgrounds.
  • 900–950 — near black. Good for headings.

Using colour utilities

bg-blue-500       /* background-color */
text-blue-700     /* color             */
border-blue-300   /* border-color      */

/* Opacity modifier */
text-blue-600/75  /* color at 75% opacity */
bg-black/50       /* black background at 50% opacity */

Typography: font size

text-xs    →  12px   text-lg  →  18px   text-4xl →  36px
text-sm    →  14px   text-xl  →  20px   text-5xl →  48px
text-base  →  16px   text-2xl →  24px   text-6xl →  60px
                     text-3xl →  30px

Typography: font weight

font-light      →  300
font-normal     →  400
font-medium     →  500
font-semibold   →  600
font-bold       →  700
font-extrabold  →  800
font-black      →  900

Typography: line-height (leading)

leading-tight    →  1.25   (headings)
leading-normal   →  1.5    (body text default)
leading-relaxed  →  1.625  (comfortable reading)
leading-loose    →  2

Typography: letter-spacing (tracking)

tracking-tight    →  -0.025em
tracking-normal   →  0em
tracking-wide     →  0.025em
tracking-widest   →  0.1em   (all-caps labels)

Text utilities

text-left    text-center    text-right
truncate     /* overflow-hidden, text-overflow: ellipsis, white-space: nowrap */
line-clamp-2 /* clamp to 2 lines with ellipsis */
uppercase    lowercase    capitalize

Sable: "Colour is not decoration — it is information. The shade tells the reader what to feel: 50 whispers. 500 speaks clearly. 900 commands attention. Learn the scale and you will never guess a hex code again."

storyBeats.speaker: Sable the Illuminator
storyBeats.text: The shade scale is your vocabulary. 50 is barely tinted — page backgrounds. 100 through 200 are subtle fills — chip backgrounds. 400 through 600 are vivid — buttons and links. 700 through 900 are deep — text and headings. Memorise those five bands and you can colour anything.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Style a blog post header. Each element has a specific typographic role:

  • .article-tag: bg-violet-100, text-violet-700, text-xs, font-semibold, rounded-full, px-3, py-1, tracking-wide
  • .article-title: text-4xl, font-bold, leading-tight, text-gray-900, mt-4
  • .article-meta: text-sm, text-gray-400, mt-2
  • .article-intro: text-lg, leading-relaxed, text-gray-700, mt-6

A large bold headline with tight line-height and dark colour. Small muted byline text. A larger intro paragraph with relaxed line-height and medium-gray colour.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: You are building a design system for a SaaS product. Explain how you would use Tailwind's colour palette to create a consistent, accessible colour system covering primary actions, semantic states (success, warning, error), and neutral text hierarchy. Which shade numbers would you reach for and why?

questions.prompt: In Tailwind's colour scale, what kind of colour is shade 50?
options: A very light, near-white tint of the colour
The most vivid, saturated version of the colour
A near-black dark shade of the colour
The neutral gray version of the colour
questions.answer: A very light, near-white tint of the colour
questions.explanation: The shade scale runs from 50 (near-white, barely tinted) up to 950 (near-black). Shade 50 is almost always a page or card background tone. Shades 400–600 are the vivid mid-range used for buttons and interactive elements. Shades 700–900 are used for text on light backgrounds.

options: Sets the text colour to emerald-600 at 50% opacity
Sets both the text colour (emerald-600) and background opacity (50%)
Sets the text colour to a 50/50 mix of emerald-600 and white
Applies emerald-600 to every other character
questions.answer: Sets the text colour to emerald-600 at 50% opacity
questions.explanation: The slash modifier (/N) appended to any colour utility sets the opacity of that specific property. text-emerald-600/50 is equivalent to setting color: rgb(5 150 105 / 0.5). This works with bg-*, border-*, and ring-* utilities too.

questions.prompt: A designer hands you Figma specs with text colours: #111827 (headings), #374151 (body), #6B7280 (captions), #9CA3AF (placeholders). Without checking the Tailwind source, which palette and shades best match?
options: gray-900, gray-700, gray-500, gray-400 — these are the exact Tailwind gray scale values
slate-900, slate-700, slate-500, slate-400 — slate is always darker than gray
zinc-950, zinc-800, zinc-600, zinc-400 — zinc skews cooler
questions.answer: gray-900, gray-700, gray-500, gray-400 — these are the exact Tailwind gray scale values
questions.explanation: Those hex values are the exact default Tailwind gray palette: gray-900=#111827, gray-700=#374151, gray-500=#6B7280, gray-400=#9CA3AF. Tailwind's designers tuned the gray scale for exactly this kind of multi-level text hierarchy. Recognising this mapping lets you translate Figma grays to class names instantly.
